column2: 12-digit Census block group GEOID (state+county+tract+block group). Read as text; join key to Census/ACS block group geometry.
Census block group name (block group; tract; county; state).
Metro area (Census CBSA) the block group belongs to.
2-letter US state abbreviation.
EPA National Walkability Index, 1 to 20. Higher = more walkable street network and destination access.
National percentile (0-100) of walkability_index across all US block groups.
Annual pedestrian deaths per 100,000 residents in the parent county (FARS 2022-2024 / 3 / county population x 100,000). Blank where FARS has no county record.
National percentile of pedestrian safety. 100 = safest (lowest death rate). Inverted so higher is always better, like every other percentile here.

The SafeStreets Walk Safety Score, 0-100. 0.7 x walkability_pctile + 0.3 x ped_safety_pctile. Answers what the EPA index cannot: is this place laid out for walking AND will walking there get you killed.
Label for safe_walk_score: Walkable and safe (>=80), Above average (>=60), Average (>=40), Below average (>=20), Car-dependent or dangerous (<20).

walkability_pctile minus ped_safety_pctile. How much a place flatters itself. Positive = built like you could walk, dangerous if you try (Las Vegas +48.6, Miami +52.9). Negative = safer than its layout suggests (Boston -15.9).
Population density, persons per square mile.
National percentile of population density.
Median household income, USD (ACS 2020-2024, as reported). Blank where ACS suppressed it.
National percentile of median household income.
Median home value, USD (ACS owner-reported, block group-level). Runs ~15-20% below market.
median_home_value / median_household_income. <=3 affordable, >=5 severely unaffordable.
National percentile, inverted: higher = more affordable (lower value-to-income).
Relative density of commercial/business activity, 0 to 1. Higher = more active commercial fabric.
National percentile of commercial activity.
Gap between walkability/density and commercial activity. Higher = walkable and dense but commercially empty.
EPA aggregate transit service frequency per square mile. Blank = no EPA record (not zero).
National percentile of transit access.
Retail employment density (EPA SLD).
Service employment density (EPA SLD).
Entertainment employment density (EPA SLD).
Retail-sector jobs in the block group.
Service-sector jobs in the block group.
Entertainment-sector jobs in the block group.
Total population (EPA SLD, ACS-derived).
Total households (EPA SLD, ACS-derived).
Spending-power component of latent retail demand (= income_pctile).
Affordability component of latent retail demand (= affordability_pctile).
0-100: unmet demand for daily-needs retail in a dense/walkable/affordable but commercially empty block group. Site-selection signal.
Most walkable (>=15.26), Above average, Below average, or Least walkable (EPA cutoffs).
True if walkability_index >= 15.26 (EPA 'most walkable' tier).
True if 0 < value_to_income_ratio <= 3.0.
True if both walkable and affordable. Only ~1% of US households live in these.
True if a curated Commercial Desert: walkable, dense, affordable, yet almost no businesses.
Pedestrian fatalities in this block group's county, 2022-2024 (NHTSA FARS, county-level).
Share of those county pedestrian deaths on surface arterials, %.
Share of those county pedestrian deaths between 6pm and 6am, %.
ZIP (ZCTA) this neighborhood maps to. Join to Zillow public research data (ZHVI/ZORI) to attach live market values.
How income was matched to this block group: exact (boundary unchanged) or nearest (transferred from the nearest current block group).
Home value divided by annual rent. Low = buying is cheap relative to renting.
National percentile of rent affordability. Higher = more affordable to rent.
True where rent exceeds 30% of median household income (HUD threshold).
National percentile of affordability against current market prices (Zillow-derived), not ACS self-reported value.
